Two separate Elo systems, both fit purely from real match results and output - no market value anywhere in either. Team power rankings is a goals-based Elo across every competition (the same rating the outcome model uses). Player Elo rates individual output (non-penalty xG + 0.7× xA per appearance) against an opponent-adjusted expectation. Pick Overall for the rating carried across seasons, or a single season for its own closed ladder - reseeded that summer at half the previous gap from 1500, counting only that season's games.

Pick any two current clubs — across leagues if you like — and play the match out. Goals are drawn from a Poisson on the Dixon-Coles expected goals for the matchup; each goal goes to a player weighted by his non-penalty xG per 90 and minutes share. Re-run for a different night, or simulate a thousand for the spread.

Pick a real team and a real season, then call every one of their league matches — win, draw or loss — one at a time. The reveal shows the actual result and what the leak-free Dixon-Coles model (fitted only on earlier matches) predicted. One wrong call ends the run. Chasing 38–0.

Every number on this page traces back to real matches, real stats and one fitted model per task — no black box, and no market value anywhere in the Elo ratings. Below is the exact arithmetic, run on today's actual data: a real upcoming fixture, a real player, a real valuation, a real rating.
